blocks.title: The Water Cycle
blocks.subtitle: How water moves between the oceans, the air and the land

blocks.text: Water is never used up. It keeps moving around the planet, changing between liquid, vapour and ice. This lesson covers the three main stages and then works through a short example.

blocks.title: Evaporation
blocks.body:
The sun heats water in oceans, lakes and rivers. Some of the liquid turns into invisible water vapour and rises into the air.

Plants add to this through transpiration, which releases water vapour from their leaves.
blocks.takeaway: Heat from the sun turns liquid water into vapour.

blocks.title: Condensation
blocks.body:
As water vapour rises it meets cooler air and loses heat. The vapour turns back into tiny liquid droplets around dust particles.

Millions of these droplets together form clouds.
blocks.takeaway: Cooling turns vapour into droplets, which form clouds.

blocks.title: Precipitation and Collection
blocks.body:
When cloud droplets merge and grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet or hail.

The water then runs off into rivers, soaks into the ground or collects in oceans and lakes. From there the cycle starts again.
blocks.takeaway: Gravity brings water back down, and the cycle repeats.

blocks.title: How much water does a lake lose in a day?
blocks.body:
A lake covers 2 square kilometres. On a warm day, evaporation removes 5 mm of water from its surface. How much water is that?

Convert everything to metres first, then multiply area by depth.
blocks.takeaway: A single lake can send about 10 million litres into the air in one day.

questions.question: Which process turns liquid water into water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens when the sun's heat gives water molecules enough energy to escape into the air as vapour.

questions.question: What causes clouds to form?
options: Water vapour cooling and condensing into droplets
questions.explanation: Rising vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets, and many droplets together make a cloud.

questions.question: Which of these is a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Precipitation is water falling from clouds, as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
